title: fix(sessions): quietly settle archived delivery endpoints
body:
Related: #174278

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading “Session delivery endpoint was replaced” warnings and blocked-delivery notices after restart when an accepted peer input belongs to otherwise unchanged archived sessions.

## User Impact

Archiving either endpoint still prevents automatic execution. Recovery retains a cancelled input receipt without adding an interruption notice. Actual session resets or replacements still block replay and record a durable notice; permission and storage failures retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The endpoint check treated `archivedAt` as an identity mismatch. Recovery now checks both exact endpoint identities first, then settles archive cancellation through the existing pending-input withdrawal owner. Debug diagnostics use `endpoint-archived`; replacement warnings use `endpoint-replaced`. This follows the existing archive contract in the session-tool docs rather than reviving archived work.

No schema, configuration, or public API changes. Production delta: +13/-3 lines (+10 net), needed to separate expected archive cancellation from genuine replacement while reusing the existing persistence owner. The archived path removes notice construction and the transcript report write; no additional cache or settlement owner.

## Evidence

- Regression before fix: archived-source and archived-target persistence cases both produced an erroneous `endpoint-replaced` report. The delayed-archive case also wrote an unwanted notice.
- After fix: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-send-recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 27 passed; 38.97 s Vitest / 44.92 s wrapper wall time, about 2.7 s in tests. Includes durable cancellation, quiet second recovery, reset/replacement, retries, consumed inputs, and permission failures.
- Before/after work per archived-only recovery: 1 blocked notice → 0; warnings → 0; 1 retained cancelled receipt in both cases; no agent dispatch. No production startup-latency claim or heavy benchmark.
- Extended the existing public `sessions_send` cold-restart test with an archived sender and pending delivery, alongside ordering, cancellation, reset, and revoked-access cases. PR CI selected both changed test files and passed all test shards and build gates. The cold-process test was not run locally because it requires a full Gateway build; retrieving its individual job log was rate-limited.
- Changed-file formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex autoreview is clean through P2. Changed-file core lint passed; the initial root-config lint was stopped because it entered plugin artifact preparation.
- No Testbox/Crabbox lease allocated, per validation instructions. [PR CI run 38934459057](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38934459057) passed on `070f755f9b45c007c4d1a6c0725f93ffb8f5f724`, including build, production/test types, lint, docs, and selected test shards. No CI retries or inherited-failure exceptions. CI durable cases: replacement 1.456 s, archived source 0.602 s, archived target 0.617 s. Hosted Codex review also completed with no findings.
